newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: UNHCR chief urges end to Zairean air raids.
newsitem.headline: UNHCR chief urges end to Zairean air raids.

text.p: Sadako Ogata, United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees, warned on Tuesday that an expanding war in eastern Zaire was threatening humanitarian work and called for an end to Zairean air raids on rebel-held towns.

"I hope this kind of attacks does not take place," she told a news conference. She said relief work in the region, where UNHCR says up to 400,000 Rwandan Hutu refugees are trapped amid fighting between rebels and Zairean troops, would suffer as a result of the intensification of military operations.

Zairean airplanes bombed the rebel-held towns of Bukavu, Shabunda and Walikale in the east on Monday. Aid workers said at least six people were killed in Bukavu. Military sources said eight were killed and scores wounded in Shabunda.
A Zairean defence ministry official in capital Kinshasa said the air raids resumed on Tuesday.
Ogata said Monday's attack had not caused much damage in Bukavu and that UNHCR were continuing work as usual.
But she added: "We will have to see how the military front goes. All our operations suffer when there is any intensification of military operations."
